answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can vote on work or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by stake and destroys part of it when an identity is proven to have double-voted or submitted fraudulent attestations. Spinning up a thousand names no longer multiplies free influence: each needs capital at risk, and coordinated cheating can burn it. Like a voyage to an island, participation has a real entry cost; nectar-sized rewards cannot make fake identities profitable unless the attacker risks more than they can gain.
